key_test: Pearson r between ERN and EPS, one row per participant (startle_type == 'error'); predicted negative; protocol says one-tailed
exclusions: none in the posted file; it holds 42 participants (ids 1-51 minus 3,4,10,18,20,28,37,40,44). The report says 8 of 51 excluded (impedance > 5 kOhm or muscle artefact) leaving 43

r_script.how: audit_harness.R: getOSFfile mapped to the local csv, external source() skipped, httr/RCurl missing -> skipped; analysis lines unchanged

agreement: all three agree on r = -.253 and p = .106 two-sided. N disagrees: table and report say 43, data and df give 42 (the report's own paired t-tests also use t(40)). Tails: the table and report label p = .11 one-tailed, but .11 is the two-sided value; the one-tailed p the protocol calls for is .053
notes: Anchored on the script and the table's r and p, which the data reproduce exactly. Two discrepancies, neither in the statistic: (1) N.R = 43 vs 42 in the data; with N = 43 the same r would give p = .1015, so the table's .11 matches 42, not 43. (2) The one-tailed label: the report writes 'r = -.25, p = .11, one-tailed', the table carries Tails.R = 1 and its own T.pval.USE.R = .053 (half of .106). The verdict on significance at .05 is the same either way (not significant), but a judge computing the protocol's one-tailed test gets p = .053, not .11.
